general.temas: The most frequently covered issues are Bolsonaro’s hospitalization, the disagreement over fossil fuels at COP31 and Delta delays in Atlanta. Also featured are the storm in Rio Grande do Sul, threats against lawmaker Talíria Petrone and the war in Ukraine. Only Gazeta do Povo highlights the institutional deadlocks in the Banco Master investigation.
general.motivo_crispacion: Political and social tension is considerable because of the death threats and racist abuse reported by lawmaker Talíria Petrone, as well as the institutional deadlocks in the Banco Master case. Internationally, Russian attacks in Ukraine and Trump’s threats against Iran are heightening tensions, while COP31 ends without an agreement among countries on fossil fuels. The coverage also includes less contentious health, culture and sports stories, which partially balance the overall picture.

Folha de S.Paulo.resumen:
- Delta flights to and from Atlanta are delayed by a technical problem.
- Lula says he suggested a meeting to Trump, Putin and Xi; Bolsonaro remains stable in intensive care.
- Roads in São Paulo are congested and police are investigating a death in Morumbi.
- A study links stopping antidepressants during pregnancy to more emergency mental health visits.
- Also featured are the premiere of a series about Sócrates and the end of the US penny.
Folha de S.Paulo.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly informative, although expressions such as “crime tribunal” and “sin tax” add drama without framing the issue as a confrontation between the people and elites.
Folha de S.Paulo.sesgo: The selection combines politics, crime and incidents, health, business and culture, with attention to Brazil and the United States. There is no discernible political slant in the wording of the headlines.

O Globo.resumen:
- A Palmeiras fan died after an incident at a São Paulo hotel following the match against Flamengo.
- The US is investigating an alleged Chinese spy linked to Nvidia’s former chief executive; a technical failure delayed Delta flights in Atlanta.
- Disagreement over phasing out fossil fuels stalled COP31 negotiations.
- The government declared a state of calamity in Tupanciretã after a deadly storm; an operation against the illegal bird trade led to three arrests.
- The front page includes stories about threats reported by lawmaker Talíria Petrone, São Paulo’s deputy mayor and Bolsonaro’s health, as well as video games, health and film.
O Globo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “keeps players glued to screens” and “sends requests soaring” add some sensationalism.
O Globo.sesgo: The selection combines crime and incidents and Brazilian politics with international news and stories of everyday interest. There is no clear ideological bias in the headlines.

O Estado de S. Paulo.resumen:
- Democrats win 258 seats and a historic majority in the US House of Representatives.
- Russian attacks near Kyiv leave at least six dead; Zelensky presses the US to release missiles.
- The failure of COP-31 poses challenges for multilateralism and the debate over fossil fuels.
- The front page includes soccer previews and Rafa Câmara joining Haas for the final races of the season.
- It also covers investments, Delta delays, health, music and video games.
O Estado de S. Paulo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although terms such as “failure” and the exclamation mark in the GTA 6 story add some emphasis; there is no discernible contrast between the people and elites.
O Estado de S. Paulo.sesgo: The selection combines international current affairs with sports and consumer information. The COP-31 headline presents the conference as a failure and describes the inclusion of fossil fuels as “unavoidable”; there is no clear overall political bias.

Gazeta do Povo.resumen:
- Trump threatens new attacks on Iran and Zelensky asks the United States for missiles after a Russian attack.
- Bolsonaro remains in intensive care, while right-wing politicians express support and ask for prayers.
- The pope celebrates Mass and has lunch with people in need; his call to a 94-year-old priest is also highlighted.
- The Banco Master investigations mark one year amid institutional blockages and deadlocks; the climate summit ends without an agreement.
- Other stories cover loneliness and dementia, longan fruit, the return to the Moon and the architecture of power in Brazil.
Gazeta do Povo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “the climate summit fails,” “scandal” and “superfruit” add drama or promotional emphasis, without a clear confrontation between the people and elites.
Gazeta do Povo.sesgo: The selection pays attention to Bolsonaro and the support of right-wing politicians, as well as the pope’s activities, taking a mostly descriptive approach. It also combines international conflicts and institutional affairs with health, science and culture stories.

CartaCapital.resumen:
- Bolsonaro remains stable in the ICU; Michelle visited him and Moraes ordered the temporary removal of his electronic ankle monitor.
- Storms in Rio Grande do Sul caused deaths and damage; a state of calamity was recognized in one municipality.
- Lawmaker Talíria Petrone reported death threats and threats of sexual violence, and a flight carrying 128 people deported from the United States arrived in Brazil.
- COP31 ended without an agreement on fossil fuels and Iran announced electricity rationing.
- The front page includes tarot, a story about Agatha Christie and an injury to a Corinthians player.
CartaCapital.motivo_populismo: The language is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “devastated” and “destroyed” add drama; there is no discernible confrontation between the people and elites.
CartaCapital.sesgo: The selection gives particular attention to Bolsonaro’s hospitalization and the effects of the storms, alongside international and entertainment news. There is no clear political bias in the wording of the headlines.

opiniones.comunista:
COP31 ends without an agreement as the phaseout of fossil fuels continues to divide countries. I see a class contradiction there: a transition left to the logic of profit guarantees neither climate protection nor a decent life for working people. We need democratic planning, collective ownership of energy and secure jobs for those who currently depend on fossil fuel industries.

The storm in Tupanciretã left five people dead and led to the recognition of a state of public calamity. I do not attribute that particular storm to climate change, but I do believe that tackling disasters requires strong public services, prevention and reconstruction that serves the population. In the face of big capital, I believe decisions on energy and infrastructure should respond to collective needs, not private profit.
opiniones.anarquista:
COP31 ended without an agreement, once again caught up in the dispute over fossil fuels. I do not trust governments alone to resolve a crisis that their own decisions also sustain. We need communities and workers who can decide how to produce energy and transform their territories, without replacing dependence on oil with obedience to new masters.

In Tupanciretã, the storm left five people dead and hundreds injured. Official recognition of the calamity may make resources available, but solidarity should not depend on a decree: mutual aid and neighborhood organizing make it possible to meet concrete needs without waiting for orders from above. That requires resources and coordination, not paternalistic charity. For me, individual and collective freedom is defended precisely there: when people can care for one another and make decisions together, without handing their fate over to parties or hierarchies.
opiniones.liberal:
The debate over the “sin tax” reminds me that predictability matters, but it is not enough. Although the distilled spirits association accepts the measure and calls for clarity on the tax rates, I question the premise: the state should not make personal choices more expensive as a substitute for individual responsibility. I prefer low taxes and stable rules that allow consumers and businesses to make decisions, take risks and answer for their actions.

The lack of an agreement at COP31 also calls for realism. Reducing emissions matters, but imposing a phaseout of fossil fuels without considering its costs can punish those who depend on affordable energy. I have more faith in competition, innovation and clear rules than in political promises disconnected from the available alternatives. A limited state should protect rights, not direct every choice.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I see the same demand in today’s news: a state that protects Brazilians and answers to them. The investigation into the man found dead in São Paulo must establish whether he was a victim of a crime tribunal. If gangs claim the power to punish, the response must be firm, with effective policing and a justice system that enforces the law.

The failure of COP31 is also a reminder that Brazil must not accept energy commitments dictated by international elites without considering its own needs. Cooperation does not mean giving up sovereignty. And the arrival of Brazilians deported from the United States reminds us that every nation has the right to strictly control its borders, while always respecting people’s dignity. I want a Brazil that defends that same right and puts the safety of its citizens first.
opiniones.centro:
The day offers an uncomfortable lesson: institutions matter especially when consensus is difficult. The failure of COP31 because of differences over fossil fuels does not justify abandoning negotiations. I would support gradual, verifiable commitments that send clear signals to investors and protect workers and communities affected by the transition. Without both, climate ambition risks remaining mere rhetoric.

I am also concerned by the reported threats and racist abuse against lawmaker Talíria Petrone. Disagreeing with a representative is legitimate; trying to intimidate her into silence attacks democracy itself. The authorities must investigate and ensure her safety. And in the face of the calamity in Tupanciretã, I welcome federal recognition: what matters now is that aid reaches those who need it quickly and transparently.
